title: The Council of Trent (1545–63)
hookLine: Catholics reform seminaries, clarify teaching, and renew the Mass

cards: What, exactly, does the Catholic Church teach, and what in its own life needs fixing? That question has been tearing the Western church apart.

To answer it, bishops arrive in a city in the mountains of northern Italy, where the road climbs toward the Alps, with theologians and representatives of kings, their books and their arguments. The council opens.
Then it breaks off. Then it meets again, and breaks off again, and meets again, over long years and more than one pope. The city's name is Trent.
Today's word is the name later given to the movement around it: Counter-Reformation.

teach.b: Counter-Reformation sounds like a punch thrown back, and part of Trent was exactly that: an answer to Luther, Zwingli and Calvin.

Some historians prefer another name, the Catholic Reformation, because some Catholics had been calling for reform of their own church before anyone left it, and because much of what Trent did was cleaning house.
First, it said clearly what Catholics hold. Scripture and tradition, received together. The sacraments, defined one by one.
How a person is made right with God: by grace, received in faith, and lived out in works.
Protestant churches answered much of this differently; Catholics receive these decrees as the teaching of a general council of the church. Second, it turned inward.
Bishops were told to live in their own dioceses and preach, instead of collecting income from far away.
Each diocese was to have a seminary, a school where future priests were trained before being sent to a parish.
After the council came a catechism and a single form of the Mass for much of the Latin church, still called the Tridentine Mass, from Trent.
Paul writes, in the King James Bible: "be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind."
Trent is what renewal looks like when a large, old institution tries it on itself: slowly, with arguments, interrupted, and then carried into the parishes by priests who had been trained first.

how: Catholics receive the Council of Trent's decrees as the teaching of an ecumenical council; seminaries for training priests, which the council called for, remain the usual path to the Catholic priesthood, and the Tridentine Mass is still celebrated in some places.

the Catholic renewal centered on the Council of Trent
a peace treaty ending the wars of religion

games.q: the Council of Trent — tap the pairs.
p: a city in the mountains of northern Italy
the other name some historians prefer

s: the council met once and finished quickly
it opened, broke off, and met again, over long years and more than one pope.
it also reformed the church's own life: bishops at home, priests trained in seminaries.
the Tridentine Mass is named after Trent
Tridentine comes from the council's city.

games.q: you're a bishop at Trent. parishes are served by priests who were never taught much. what do you vote for?
o: leave it to each priest to learn on his own.
a seminary in each diocese to train them first.
close the parishes that have no good priest.
games.why: the council called for a seminary in each diocese, so future priests would be trained before they were sent out.

practice: Take one of Trent's quieter changes: bishops were told to live among their people.
Bring to mind one thing you look after from a distance, a friendship kept up only by text, a group you belong to on paper, and picture what showing up in person would look like.
If you pray, ask for help to take that step; if you don't, hold it in mind and let it settle.

wordCard.voice: Counter-Reformation. The name later given to the Catholic answer to the Reformation, centered on the Council of Trent, which both restated Catholic teaching and reformed the church's own life. Some call it the Catholic Reformation.

orig.note: Latin: the Council of Trent, from Tridentum, the city's Latin name. Tridentine comes from it.

carryVoice: Your line: reform from within. Slowly, with arguments, and from the inside. See you tomorrow.
